question: A particle projected vertically upward reaches, at the end of \(t\) seconds, an elevation of \(s\) feet where \(s=160t-16t^2.\) The highest elevation is:
solution:
To find the greatest height, rewrite the formula as a constant minus a nonnegative square:
\[
\begin{aligned}
s&=160t-16t^2\\
&=-16(t^2-10t)\\
&=-16\bigl((t-5)^2-25\bigr)\\
&=400-16(t-5)^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
Since \((t-5)^2\ge0\), the elevation cannot exceed \(400\) feet. Equality occurs at \(t=5\) seconds, which is an allowed time after launch. Therefore the highest elevation is \(\boxed{400\text{ feet}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
